question: Gemini 4's idea 3 (against DESIGN_PROXY section 2): can the final-block ledger be recovered from the top-M output logprobs alone, and does a sparse WDD prior (OMP in logit space) beat the minimum-norm reconstruction when M <= D?
design: wikitext-2 test positions; reference = 16-word OMP of unit(y - ybar) over the native rows as the unembedding reads them; R1 min-norm deviation from [ybar; c0] then OMP (float64), R2 OMP in R^M over restricted centred signatures; controls: another position's observation, random tokens instead of the top M, the reference vs another position's reference; M = 20, 64, 256, 1024, 2048, all. Pythia-160m, Pythia-410m, Qwen2.5-0.5B. Prior art for M > D+1: Finlayson et al. 2024, Carlini et al. 2024.
smoke: Pythia-160m (D=768), 32 positions: R1 exact at M=1024 and above (cosine 1.000, Jaccard 1.000); below D the state cosine is 0.27/0.40/0.62 at M=20/64/256 but the ledger Jaccard only 0.02/0.04/0.06 (top word 0.22/0.25/0.41); R2 worse than R1 at every M (Jaccard 0.00-0.05); the unembedding-side ledger and the hidden-state ledger share Jaccard 0.22; 0.56 of the reference words come from the last four of twelve blocks.

B1.text: at M = 20, OMP in logit space recovers the reference ledger's largest word at 50 percent or more of positions

B2.text: at M = 20, OMP in logit space beats its other-position control by 0.10 or more in support Jaccard

B3.text: the sparse prior helps when underdetermined: OMP in logit space beats the minimum-norm reconstruction in Jaccard at both M = 64 and M = 256

B4.text: above D+1 logprobs (M = 2048) the minimum-norm reconstruction recovers the state (cosine 0.99 or more) and the ledger (Jaccard 0.95 or more)

B5.text: the ledger as the unembedding reads it agrees with the usual hidden-state ledger (Jaccard 0.5 or more)

B6.text: 60 percent or more of the reference ledger's words come from the last four blocks

status: fixed before the full runs; smokes on Pythia-160m (plumbing; seen before these were fixed, and reflected in the guesses)
